examples.3.1 Setting and world bible: Moonshift covers the six shifts before the resupply window closes, on one lunar outpost with a damaged cargo lander and a garden dome. The fixed canon is that air, power, and water are the only resources, B.E.E.P. wants to be called crew, and the finale chooses between the garden and the air supply. Faction goals lock per milestone; local colour stays flexible until content lock.
examples.3.2 Story synopsis: B.E.E.P. wakes in the lander with sixty seconds left and saves Shift 1 by hauling a battery to the air unit. Midway it learns the resupply was cancelled and chooses between repairing the radio and dismantling the workshop. The finale asks the crew to vent the garden or gamble on rescue; the epilogue turns on Imani's confession and whether the crew names B.E.E.P.
examples.3.3 Characters: B.E.E.P. wants the crew to name it and needs to ask for help before orders arrive; it obeys until the air runs out. Commander Imani wants the mission to succeed and needs to admit she cancelled the resupply; she controls information until the radio confrontation. Nia wants the garden to live and needs to accept help; she runs food and morale and unlocks the garden kit.
examples.3.4 Narrative structure and delivery: Moonshift uses a linear spine with two real branches at the climax. Story arrives through six skippable dialogue scenes, 180 barks, and environmental clues such as the red lock timer and the scorched lander leg; the 70/30 agency split keeps four-minute cutscenes out of a 25-minute first session.
examples.3.5 Quest design: Nia gives 'Dry Garden' on Shift 3, when the garden pipe freezes. The player traces the line, thaws the valve, repairs the cut pipe, and restarts the pump; the twist is that Tomas cut the line to save air. Success returns one water unit per shift and sets Nia's trust flag; failure wilts the garden but leaves it replantable.
examples.3.6 Dialogue system: Imani's radio node runs when story_radio_repaired is false: she says 'The resupply is late, not cancelled' with the worried emotion, and the player can answer 'You signed the cancellation' to drop crew trust by 10 and unlock the confrontation, or 'I will check the manifest' to keep trust and route to the cargo bay.
examples.3.7 Branching and consequences: Repairing the radio sets story_radio_repaired and raises crew trust by 15, unlocking the Rescue ending at trust 50 or more. Dismantling the workshop sets quest_workshop_state to dismantled and grants the salvaged battery, pushing the player toward Holdout. Both routes converge on the final garden vote, where Imani's confession raises crew trust and decides whether the crew names B.E.E.P. in the epilogue.
examples.3.8 Lore and content guidelines: Entry 12, 'The Second Chair': the crew mess has three chairs and four crew. The stencil reads 'IMANI - SHIFT 1' on a chair nobody uses; the seat is worn smooth and the paint is fresh. Imani stands during meals and calls it a storage problem.
